questions.question: The equilibrium of $x_{t+2}-2.5x_{t+1}+x_t=0$ is $x^*=0$, and the solution with $x_0=2$, $x_1=1$ is $x_t=2(0.5)^t\to0$. Is the equilibrium asymptotically stable (asymptotically stable: every solution converges to the equilibrium $x^*$, whatever the initial values)?
options: Yes: a solution converging to $x^*$ shows asymptotic stability.
Yes: the root $0.5$ has modulus below $1$, which suffices.
No: most initial values excite the root $2$ and then diverge.
No: no solution of this equation ever converges to $x^*=0$.

questions.question: A constant-coefficient equation with $p(1)\ne0$ has characteristic roots $r_1,\ldots,r_k$. Which condition on the roots is equivalent to asymptotic stability (asymptotically stable: every solution converges to the equilibrium $x^*$, whatever the initial values)?
options: $\operatorname{Re}r_i<0$ for every root
$\lvert\operatorname{Re}r_i\rvert<1$ for every root
$\lvert r_i\rvert\le1$ for every root
$\lvert r_i\rvert<1$ for every root

questions.question: An equation has the double characteristic root $r=0.9$, so its deviations from $x^*$ contain the term $t\,(0.9)^t$. Does the factor $t$ prevent asymptotic stability?
options: No: $t(0.9)^t\to0$, since geometric decay beats the linear factor.
Yes: $t\to\infty$, so $t(0.9)^t$ grows without bound.
Yes: a repeated root always makes an equation unstable.
No, but only because $0.9$ is positive; a double root $-0.9$ would fail.

questions.question: For $x_{t+1}=-x_t+b$ (first order, $a=-1$), the equilibrium is $x^*=b/2$. Is it asymptotically stable (asymptotically stable: every solution converges to the equilibrium $x^*$, whatever the initial values)?
options: Yes: the coefficient $a=-1$ has $\lvert a\rvert\le1$.
No: $x_t=x^*+(-1)^t(x_0-x^*)$ is a two-cycle unless $x_0=x^*$.
Yes: the path oscillates around $x^*$ and so converges to it.
No: there is no equilibrium, since $1-a=0$.

questions.question: An asymptotically stable equation has characteristic roots $0.9$ and $-0.5$. Which number governs how fast deviations from $x^*$ eventually shrink per period?
options: $0.5$, the smallest root modulus
$0.45$, the product of the moduli
$0.9$, the largest root modulus
$0.4$, the sum of the roots

questions.question: For $x_{t+1}=-0.5\,x_t+6$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, with $x_0=0$, how does the solution behave?
options: It converges to $4$, alternating above and below $4$.
It converges to $4$ monotonically from below.
It converges to $6$, alternating around $6$.
It diverges, since the coefficient $-0.5$ is negative.

questions.question: Apply the second-order test ($\lvert a_0\rvert<1$ and $\lvert a_1\rvert<1+a_0$) to $x_{t+2}-0.5x_{t+1}+0.06x_t=b$. Is the equilibrium asymptotically stable?
options: No: $a_1=-0.5$ is negative, which the test forbids.
No: the test needs $\lvert a_1\rvert<a_0$, and $0.5>0.06$.
Yes, but only if $b=0$, since $b$ affects stability.

questions.question: The equation $x_{t+2}+0.64\,x_t=b$ has characteristic roots $\pm0.8\,\mathrm{i}$. How do deviations from the equilibrium behave?
options: Oscillation with constant amplitude, as roots are imaginary
Explosive oscillation, amplitude growing like $1.25^t$
Monotone decay, since the roots have real part $0$
Damped oscillation, amplitude shrinking like $0.8^t$

questions.question: Using the necessary condition $p(1)>0$, decide whether the equilibrium of $x_{t+2}-1.5x_{t+1}+0.4x_t=b$, with characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^2-1.5r+0.4$, is asymptotically stable (every solution converges to it).
options: Yes: $\lvert a_0\rvert=0.4<1$ is already enough.
No: $p(1)=-0.1<0$ violates a necessary condition.
Yes: $p(1)\ne0$, so the equilibrium is unique.
Undecided: necessary conditions say nothing when they fail.

questions.question: For $x_{t+1}=1.2\,x_t-1$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, the equilibrium is $x^*=5$. What happens to the solution starting at $x_0=5.1$?
options: It converges to $5$, since it starts close to $5$.
It stays at $5.1$, since it is close to an equilibrium.
It moves away from $5$, as $x_t-5=0.1\cdot1.2^t$ grows.
It converges to $-1$, the value of the input.

questions.question: For $x_{t+2}+2x_{t+1}+0.5x_t=b$, both necessary conditions hold: $\lvert a_0\rvert=0.5<1$ and $p(1)=3.5>0$. Is the equilibrium asymptotically stable?
options: Yes: both necessary conditions together are sufficient.
Yes: $p(1)>0$ alone guarantees all roots inside the unit circle.
No: a root is $-1-\sqrt{0.5}\approx-1.71$, outside the unit circle.
No: $p(1)>1$ shows a root larger than $1$.

questions.question: Suppose the characteristic polynomial of a constant-coefficient equation satisfies $p(1)=0$. Why can the equation not be asymptotically stable (asymptotically stable: every solution converges to the equilibrium $x^*$, whatever the initial values)?
options: $p(1)=0$ forces all roots to have modulus exactly $1$.
$p(1)=0$ makes every solution grow linearly in $t$.
It can be: this depends only on the other roots.
$r=1$ is a root, so constant deviations never die out.

questions.question: For $x_{t+2}-0.5x_{t+1}+0.06x_t=b$, the constant $b$ is raised from $3$ to $30$. What happens to the equilibrium and to its stability?
options: $x^*=b/p(1)$ is multiplied by $10$; stability is unchanged.
$x^*$ is unchanged; stability may be lost for large $b$.
$x^*$ is multiplied by $10$; stability is lost because $b>1$.
Both change, since the roots depend on $b$.

questions.question: For $x_{t+2}-x_{t+1}+a_0x_t=b$ with real $a_0\ne0$, for which values of $a_0$ is the equilibrium asymptotically stable, by the test $\lvert a_0\rvert<1$, $\lvert a_1\rvert<1+a_0$?
options: Exactly for $-1<a_0<1$
Exactly for $0<a_0<1$
Exactly for $\tfrac{1}{4}<a_0<1$
Exactly for $0<a_0\le1$

questions.question: The equation $x_{t+2}-3.5x_{t+1}+1.5x_t=0$ has roots $3$ and $0.5$, so it is unstable. With $x_0=4$, which value of $x_1$ makes the solution converge to $0$?
options: None, since the equation is unstable

questions.question: The equation $x_{t+3}-0.5x_{t+2}+0.25x_{t+1}-0.125x_t=1$ has $p(r)=(r-0.5)(r^2+0.25)$. Is its equilibrium asymptotically stable, and what is it?
options: Asymptotically stable, with $x^*=1.6$
Unstable, since $p$ has nonreal roots
Asymptotically stable, with $x^*=1$
Asymptotically stable, with $x^*=8/7$

questions.question: For $p(r)=(r-0.5)(r^2+1.21)$, a student finds the only real root $0.5$ and declares the equilibrium asymptotically stable. What is wrong?
options: Nothing: nonreal roots do not affect convergence, only real ones.
Roots $\pm1.1\mathrm{i}$ have modulus $1.1>1$, so oscillations grow.
The real root $0.5$ is too close to $1$ for stability.
The stability test needs $p(1)<0$, but here $p(1)>0$.

questions.question: Why is $p(1)>0$ a necessary condition for asymptotic stability of an equation with real coefficients and monic characteristic polynomial $p(r)=\prod_i(r-r_i)$?
options: $p(1)=\prod_i\lvert r_i\rvert$, which is positive when all roots lie inside the unit circle.
$p(1)$ is the equilibrium $x^*$, which must be positive for a stable equation.
$p(1)=-(r_1+\cdots+r_k)$, which is positive when all roots are small.
$p(1)=\prod_i(1-r_i)$: real factors are positive and conjugate pairs give $\lvert1-r\rvert^2>0$.

questions.question: For $x_{t+2}-0.2x_{t+1}-0.8x_t=3$, check $\lvert a_0\rvert<1$ and $\lvert a_1\rvert<1+a_0$. What is the correct conclusion?
options: Asymptotically stable: $\lvert a_0\rvert=0.8<1$ and $\lvert a_1\rvert=0.2<1$.
Asymptotically stable: the roots $1$ and $-0.8$ satisfy $\lvert r\rvert\le1$.
Not asymptotically stable: $\lvert a_1\rvert=0.2$ is not below $1+a_0=0.2$.
Asymptotically stable, with equilibrium $x^*=3/p(1)=3$ as the limit.

questions.question: For $x_{t+1}=(2-k)\,x_t+1$ with real parameter $k$, for which $k$ is there an asymptotically stable equilibrium?
options: Exactly for $k<3$
Exactly for $1<k<3$
Exactly for $1\le k\le3$
Exactly for $k>1$
